title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum and return its sum.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum 6.

hints: At each index, decide: extend the previous subarray, or start a new one here. Kadane's algorithm.

testCases.description: All negative — answer is the least negative single element

optimalSolution.approach: Kadane's algorithm: track the best sum ending at the current index (either extend or restart), and the best seen overall.

followUpQuestions: Why does 'restart if current sum goes negative' work — what's the intuition?
How would you also return the actual subarray, not just its sum?
Can you solve this with divide-and-conquer instead? What's its complexity?
interviewerNotes: Classic DP-vs-greedy framing question. Watch for candidates who default to brute-force O(n^2) and never reach Kadane's without a nudge — a fair signal on pattern recognition, not obscure knowledge.
